title: Higgsfield Global Film Festival 2026: $500,000 Grand Prize Goes to Listen to Meh
excerpt: Higgsfield Global Film Festival 2026 announces its $1 million winners: Listen to Meh, Fukushima, The Field Agent, and The Tortoise and the Hare.
imageAlt: Listen to Meh, winner of the Higgsfield Global Film Festival 2026
heroCaption: Listen to Meh — Higgsfield Global Film Festival 2026 Grand Prize winner.
body: Higgsfield has announced the results of its 2026 Global Film Festival, a competition for original AI-generated short films. Fourteen films were awarded out of a $1,000,000 prize pool, split across three jury-ranked prizes, an Audience Choice Award, and ten Honorable Mentions. The festival drew 5,000 final film submissions from 176 countries.

The $500,000 first prize went to Listen to Meh, by Argentina's Purga Studio — a story about a gaucho whose routine is repeatedly interrupted by a sheep that keeps returning to his roof. Filmmaker Alex Proyas, serving on the jury, called the film "funny, moving, thoughtful and visually inventive."

Second place and $200,000 went to Fukushima, about a veteran nuclear engineer confronting an unfolding disaster. Third place and $100,000 went to The Field Agent, and the $100,000 Audience Choice Award went to The Tortoise and the Hare, an animated tale about a group of rabbits hunting for a legendary golden tortoise.
Ten further films received Honorable Mentions worth $10,000 each, including FIX, ROAR and The Elevator.
The full list of winners and Honorable Mentions, with posters and director credits, is on AIMB's Higgsfield Global Film Festival page.

contentBlocks.text: On November 1, 2026, the Higgsfield Global Film Festival announced its winners, concluding an international competition dedicated to AI-generated filmmaking. The festival distributed a total prize pool of $1 million across fourteen recognized films, from three jury-ranked prizes and an Audience Choice Award to ten Honorable Mentions.
Listen to Meh Wins the $500,000 Grand Prize

The festival's biggest award went to Listen to Meh, created by Argentina's Purga Studio. The film follows a gaucho whose ordinary routine is repeatedly interrupted by a sheep that mysteriously returns to his roof. Its combination of humor, thoughtful storytelling and distinctive visual direction impressed the jury. Filmmaker Alex Proyas described the film as “funny, moving, thoughtful and visually inventive.”

Fukushima, The Field Agent and Audience Choice

Fukushima received the $200,000 second-place prize. Its story follows a veteran engineer confronting an impending disaster at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant. Third place and $100,000 went to The Field Agent, an offbeat story about a drive-in cinema devotee who finds himself with a mission. South Korea's The Tortoise and the Hare won the $100,000 Audience Choice Award for its animated rabbit adventure.

contentBlocks.text: Ten More Films Receive Honorable Mentions

The festival also awarded ten Honorable Mentions, each worth $10,000. Among the standout entries are FIX, with its imaginative paper-crafted world; ROAR, a visually striking dinosaur story; and The Elevator, an increasingly surreal journey through unexpected worlds. Together, the selected films show how widely AI filmmakers are experimenting with visual style, genre and storytelling.

What the Festival Means for AI Filmmaking

The festival reported 55,628 participants, more than 67,000 projects started, and 5,000 final films submitted from 176 countries. Its winners demonstrate the range of creative directions available to filmmakers working with generative tools, from understated comedy to carefully built fantasy worlds.

Beyond the prize money, the competition places emphasis on the people behind the films: their ideas, editorial decisions, sound design and ability to build an engaging story. As the medium develops, that balance between technology and authorship becomes increasingly important.
